$comment: The approved-provider record for T0.1's network scripts. PROOF_STANDARD.md Version 3 §11
requires a two-provider claim to use providers with DIFFERENT OPERATORS, and requires that
independence to be checked against a machine-readable record rather than asserted in prose.
URLs are NOT stored here. A provider's URL is supplied by the environment variable named in
'urlEnv' so that a key-bearing endpoint is never committed. Each run records the sanitized
canonical host it actually resolved to and refuses to proceed if that host is not the one this
record approves for that provider id.
'operator' must be a real, checkable operator identity. 'unknown' is honest and is exactly why
a pair containing it yields proofLevel 'one-domain' rather than 'two-distinct-operators'.

providers.archiveSupport: measured: eth_call served at 43.6 days (8/8), refused at 50.8 days (0/8), 2026-09-22

providers.operatorEvidence: a named company with its own account, quota and billing relationship; the only provider in this project with an established distinct operator

providers.notes: Recorded so it is not retried by a later reader. Free tier cannot serve this workload.

pairPolicy.twoDistinctOperators: Both providers must have a non-null 'operator' that is not 'unknown', and the two operators must differ. Only then may evidence carry proofLevel 'two-distinct-operators'.
pairPolicy.oneDomain: Any other pair. Evidence carries proofLevel 'one-domain', which PROOF_STANDARD.md Version 3 §1b states does not satisfy that section. A run invoked as proof exits non-zero with NOT_INDEPENDENT.
pairPolicy.hostCheck: The resolved host of each provider's URL must equal the 'host' recorded here for that id, or the run fails. This keeps a key out of the repository while making a swapped endpoint visible to a reviewer.
